header: The electric-car window, in two tabs (the charging time now carries WHAT IT COSTS too: tariff.ts, official figures, a ceiling or the person's own rate): "Charging time" (below) and "EV specifications explained" (EvGuide.tsx). CHARGING TIME: the battery size, the charge to start and end at, what the car accepts on AC and DC; the answer is a table of how long each kind of charger takes, with what the words mean underneath. It all runs in the browser (src/tools/ev/ev.ts); nothing is stored or sent. The times are approximate, and the card says so.

doc: The electric-car window: two tabs, the charging-time estimate and the plain-words guide to the words of a spec sheet.

behaviours: the window has two tabs, Charging time and EV specifications explained, and opens on the charging time
the guide tab draws the two numbers, the jump list and six sections, each with its terms
it says the plain things: kWh is the tank, kW the engine, 100 kW is 134 bhp or 136 PS, the motor is an AC motor, one socket takes AC and DC
the worked example is computed: 110 kW is 148 bhp or 150 PS, a 60 kWh battery goes about 300 km, and 10% to 90% on 7.4 kW AC adds 48 kWh in about 7 h 12 min
the Blade section links its sources (BYD, Autocar India, Autocar Professional, S&P) with the words under 'What it says'
the guide never claims a thing it should not: no price in rupees and no named car's range
every charger row carries a cost, 'up to' the ceiling: 12 rows of chargers, each with its rupees
the first AC row (3.3 kW) and the first DC row cost what the sum says: 32 kWh added from 40 kWh, 10% to 90%: AC by day about ₹ 302, DC by day about ₹ 556
each row says its sum: units drawn × the rate, with its two parts
the card has the time-of-day pills (day, evening, night) and the own-rate box, and says plainly that it is a ceiling before GST and land cost
the sources are on the card: the WBERC order of 20 March 2025 and the Ministry of Power guidelines of 17 September 2024, with the validity and the review
the time of day is a radio group of three, not tabs (the window keeps exactly two tabs)
the guide tab still says nothing of price (the cost lives on the time tab only)
the rate chart is on the card, with a column for each time of day and a row for AC, for DC and for home
AC: 8.50, 10.00 and 9.50 (electricity + service, by day, evening and night)
the chart says it is a ceiling before GST and land cost, names both sources' figures and that the 4 to 5 pm hour is priced as night, and that one ceiling covers all AC and all DC chargers
home: the domestic rate applies, and the box for the rate on the bill is pointed to
the chosen time of day is marked in the chart (the day, by default), and nothing is marked when the person has typed a rate
the guide tab has no chart
